title: Into the Deep
subtitle: The sea surface down to the Challenger Deep
sourceNote: Challenger Deep depth from the 2019 Five Deeps Expedition sounding, 10,935 m.

waypoints.name: Recreational diving limit
waypoints.body: As deep as a recreational diver is trained to go. Red light has already vanished, so blood looks green down here.

waypoints.name: The end of the sunlight zone
waypoints.body: Below this there is not enough light for photosynthesis anywhere on Earth. Ninety percent of marine life lives in the water above you.

waypoints.name: The deepest scuba dive
waypoints.body: Ahmed Gabr, 2014. Twelve minutes to descend, and fifteen hours to come back up safely.

waypoints.name: The midnight zone
waypoints.body: No sunlight reaches here at all, ever. Almost all the light in this water is made by the animals themselves.

waypoints.name: The deepest whale dive
waypoints.body: A Cuvier's beaked whale, recorded in 2014, holding its breath for two hours and seventeen minutes.

waypoints.name: The average ocean depth
waypoints.body: The mean depth of the world ocean. Half the planet's surface is seafloor deeper than three kilometres.

waypoints.name: The Titanic
waypoints.body: The wreck sits here in the dark, four hundred miles off Newfoundland. Nobody found it until 1985.

waypoints.name: The abyssal plain
waypoints.body: The flattest place on Earth. Soft sediment, near-freezing water and almost total stillness for thousands of kilometres.

waypoints.name: The hadal zone
waypoints.body: Named after Hades. Found only inside ocean trenches, which are less than one percent of the seafloor.

waypoints.name: Everest, upside down
waypoints.body: If you dropped Mount Everest in here, its summit would still be two kilometres beneath you.

waypoints.name: The Challenger Deep
waypoints.body: The bottom. Eleven hundred atmospheres of pressure. Fewer people have been here than have walked on the Moon.
